action: Insurance upload rescue after a 24-hour stall
what_to_do: After Fitness passes, deep-link the remaining upload; offer a scheduled support callback after 24h without upload. Interview a sample about document availability.
risks: Some captains lack valid insurance; never waive verification. Reminder fatigue, agent cost, and worse conversion among recovered users.
measure: Randomized holdout among 24h stalls; incremental Insurance uploads and A2O within signup D30, R2A D30, cost/incremental approval, invalid-document rate and complaints.

action: Repair image-quality failures on low-tier devices
working: Sum over RC/Fitness/Insurance: latest unresolved quality failures / 5 × 50% additional passes × vehicle-standardized low-device downstream A2O
what_to_do: Pilot guided capture, legibility/blur feedback, resumable upload and assisted recapture. Start with RC; extend the same component to Fitness and Insurance.
risks: No image pixels or upload-failure logs are supplied; diagnose first. False rejections, latency on low-tier devices, manual review load, privacy and fraud escape.
measure: Randomize low-tier captains before the first RC upload; subgroup first-pass rates, failed attempts, A2O/R2A D30, p95 latency, review minutes and audited false accepts.

action: Hold the 5× campaign request; run an RC-stage randomized test
working: No causal forecast booked. Conditional full-reach scenario: 1160.2 new recipients/month × 0.0417 = 48.4 approvals/month.
what_to_do: Randomize about 3,856 RC clearers 1:1 to early WA002 or holdout, suppress crossovers, reconcile click/delivery telemetry; then scale only if incremental economics pass.
risks: Unmeasured targeting, overlap with other interventions, spam/opt-outs and unknown repeated-touch returns; suppressing current sends has opportunity cost.
measure: Pre-register assignment-based A2O at 30 days after RC randomization, R2A D30, delivery and complaints, actual spend and cost per incremental approval.
